meta.title: Our Old Town Program
meta.textType: functional: a program with a key and a map, and a club talk

paragraphs: On Thursday, February eleventh, the Explorers met in the school library for the club hour. Teacher Kim gave each pair a program and a map for Saturday's walk in the old town. Lily sat with May. Leo sat with Mia. The program had instructions at the top. The children read them first. "Start with the key," said Teacher Kim, "because the key explains the little pictures." In a small box under the map, a flag meant the start of the walk. A camera meant a photo stop, and a pencil meant a quiz stop. A cup meant the tea shop. Five places on the map were joined by a dotted path.

Teacher Kim read the times out loud. "First, we meet at the old gate at nine o'clock," she said. "Next, we walk to the old well. We arrive at half past nine." "After that, we visit the gallery at ten o'clock." "Then we go to the stone wall at half past ten." "Finally, we have a drink at the tea shop at eleven o'clock." The walk takes two hours. The ticket includes a cold juice for every child.

Then Teacher Kim held up the last line of the program. "Bring your school ID card, a bottle of water, a hat, and a pencil case with two pencils." Lily put her school ID card next to her pencil case on the table. "Why do we need an ID card?" asked May. "Every child shows the card at the gallery door," said Teacher Kim. Mia wrote down the four things in her notebook.

"Which stop has the quiz?" asked May. Lily found the pencil on the gallery line of the program. "The gallery has an exhibition of old photos," said Teacher Kim. "At the quiz stop, each pair writes down the year of one photo." "I prefer the gallery, because I like old photos," said Leo. "I like the well best," said Mia, "because taking photos there is fun." Teacher Kim smiled. "Every stop has something to see," she said.

"The program gives all the details of the day," said Teacher Kim. "The bus leaves the school gate at a quarter past eight." "The tea shop is crowded on Saturdays, so please stay with your partner." "Every parent signs the note before Saturday." May wrote the bus time on her program in big letters.

Leo looked at the map once more. "Five stops and one quiz," he said. "That is a good plan." "We need good weather, too," said Mia. Lily put her program carefully in her bag. Then she looked at the dotted path on her map and smiled.
